sources.title: Closure of Government Schools — Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1374
sources.locator: PDF page4, Annexure I; pages5–6, Annexure II
sources.summary: Annexure I reports government-school stock counts for five academic years by state/UT. Annexure II reports government-school stock counts for all Uttar Pradesh districts. India government schools: 1,022,386 in 2021-22 and 1,005,245 in 2025-26. NEP paragraph 7.4 says consolidation should only proceed when access is unaffected.
limitations: The answer provides stock counts, not a school-by-school closure or merger register.
Districts are not cities or school catchments.
No matched population series or causal impact evaluation is provided.
Reported by states/UTs through UDISE+.

sources.title: Declining Enrolment of Students in Government Schools in Uttar Pradesh — Lok Sabha Question 2445
sources.locator: PDF page1, answer(e)
sources.summary: Provides approved central and actual released central shares for Uttar Pradesh Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI for three financial years. Shamli district government-school counts rise from 621 in 2021-22 to 623 in 2025-26.
limitations: The requested district spending is answered with state-level approved/released figures; do not label these district spending.
Releases are not expenditure, audited utilisation, or money received by an individual school.
Annexures contain government-school counts, not verified closure events.

sources.title: Ministry of Education releases UDISE+ 2024-25 report
sources.publisher: Ministry of Education / Press Information Bureau
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports 104,125 single-teacher schools and 7,993 zero-enrolment schools in 2024-25. Reports total teachers 10,122,420. Reports computer access in 64.7% and internet in 63.5% of schools.
limitations: National aggregate with mixed management categories; not a city-level finding.
A zero-enrolment school is not necessarily a closed school.
2025-26 official parliamentary school-count data is newer.

sources.title: Report on UDISE+ 2023-24 — existing structure
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Separates government, government-aided, private unaided recognised, and other schools. Reports that student-wise collection from 2022-23 is not strictly comparable with earlier aggregate reporting for several education indicators.
limitations: Historical methodology reference; not latest school data.
Population denominator moderation can affect ratio comparisons.
UDISE listing alone does not confer recognition.

sources.title: AISHE Final Reports
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Lists 2023-24 and 2022-23 final reports and Excel files.
limitations: Index page is a discovery source, not a transaction or district funding ledger.

sources.title: Union Ministry releases AISHE 2022-23 and 2023-24 reports
sources.publisher: Ministry of Education / Press Information Bureau
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: For 2023-24, 59,533 of 64,756 registered HEIs participated. Higher education enrolment is reported as 4.50 crore in 2023-24. GER is 30 in 2023-24 and uses ages 18-23 population projections based on Census 2011.
limitations: Participation is voluntary and data is self-reported by institutions.
Registration, survey response and estimated enrolment have different denominators.
Report reference period differs from publication date.

sources.title: AISHE Report 2023-24
sources.publisher: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: 48,246 colleges were registered and 46,468 responded. Of responding colleges, 17.1% were government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided. Contains state tables for private/government colleges and district distribution.
limitations: Responding-college percentages must not be applied as exact counts to all registered colleges.
Institution prevalence is not a funding share.

sources.title: Chhattisgarh Samagra Shiksha 2025-26 revised PAB minutes
sources.publisher: Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education
sources.locator: Prose paragraphs 3–4 and financial section 2
sources.summary: Approved annual work plan: ₹232,029.17 lakh including ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover. Planned central share to be released: ₹112,900.28 lakh; corresponding state share ₹75,267.52 lakh. Supplementary ICT labs and smart classrooms approval: ₹14,133.80 lakh.
limitations: Supersedes sections of earlier 9 May 2025 minutes; preserve version history.
The section heading says Actual Release, but the line explicitly says to be released: classify as planned/approved, not actual disbursement.
Opening balances and spillover make the approved plan different from fresh allocations.
OCR affects table layout; use explicit prose figures and reconcile original PDF before bulk extraction.
Origin PDF returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-06; preserve indexed-text access status and locate replacement archive before treating as live-verified.

sources.title: Cabinet approves PM SHRI Schools
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Total project cost ₹27,360 crore, including central share ₹18,128 crore, over five years. Targets more than 14,500 existing schools managed by central/state/UT/local government. Selection uses eligibility checks and challenge mode.
limitations: Multi-year programme outlay is not current-year expenditure or total India education funding.
Not a grant programme for all private unaided schools.
National targets do not verify city-level awards.

sources.title: PM Schools for Rising India — scheme information
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: At the page's update, 12,079 schools had been selected through four phases. Confirms ₹27,360 crore total and ₹18,128 crore central project cost.
limitations: Selection snapshot is dated November 2024 and must not be labelled current in October 2026.

sources.title: PM-USHA Guidelines
sources.publisher: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Covers government and government-aided higher education institutions of states/UTs. Gives priority to focus districts and defines components and eligibility.
limitations: Eligibility and programme scope do not establish that an institution has received funding.
Historical AISHE figures in the guidelines are not current counts.

sources.title: PM-USHA: Building Stronger Institutions for a Knowledge-Driven Future
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Education
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Scheme outlay ₹12,926.10 crore for 2023-24 to 2025-26. First two PAB meetings approved 440 units worth ₹5,613.12 crore. FY 2025-26 budget stated as ₹1,815 crore. Eight new model degree college units approved across Nagaland (4), Manipur (2), Meghalaya (2), totaling ₹119.98 crore.
limitations: Outlay, PAB approvals and annual budget are distinct stages and cannot be added together.
A unit is not necessarily a unique institution.
Snapshot is May 2025; not live allocations.

sources.title: Population Projections for India and States 2011–2036
sources.publisher: National Commission on Population, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; government mirror by Chhattisgarh DES
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Uses Census 2011, SRS fertility/mortality and migration assumptions. Projects total population increase and a decline in the national population aged 5–14 during 2011–2036.
limitations: Projections are model-based rather than new census observations.
Total population growth cannot substitute for school-age population growth.
District/city downscaling requires separate validation.
Mirrored copies surfaced differing summary totals; numeric population claims are intentionally omitted until document edition provenance is reconciled.

sources.title: Five years, 10 states: Where India's government school count fell the most
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports uneven state-level net school-count reductions and warns against reading stock differences as a simple linear demographic story.
limitations: Secondary lead, not proof of individual closures or wrongdoing.
Do not import the headline as a closure-event count.

sources.title: No merger for schools with 50 or more students as Uttar Pradesh government revises plan
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports minister's clarification excluding schools with 50 or more students and schools farther than 1km from pairing. Reports minister saying UDISE codes remain unchanged, buildings may host Bal Vatikas, and original classes can resume if enrolment/capacity warrants.
limitations: Reported policy and explanation, not independent verification of implementation.
Do not turn nearly 10,000 proposed pairings into confirmed permanent closures.
Preserved codes mean stock series can miss changes in where teaching takes place.

sources.title: UP govt tells HC: No merger if school has over 50 students, 1km distance
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports extension of interim status quo for school pairing in Sitapur until 1 September 2025. Reports government assurances on enrolment/distance and court clarification that interim order does not affect overall policy.
limitations: Historical interim procedural status, not current case disposition.
Later court orders must be obtained before stating present legality or operative stay.

sources.title: Karnataka rolls out project to merge government schools with KPS magnet schools
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports a seven-school pilot linked to Honganuru KPS. Quotes circular instructions on student transfers and transport arrangements. Reports concern from educationists/student organisations about rural access.
limitations: Underlying circular not retrieved in this pass.
Announced/proposed state scale is not completed implementation.
Allegation that a much larger number of schools would close is not adopted as a fact.

sources.title: Government urged to withdraw order allowing merger of low-enrolment schools
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports minister's statement that government has no plans to shut any government school. Reports AIDSO seeking withdrawal of a merger clause and a written assurance.
limitations: Capture minister's denial alongside access concerns.
School closure, transfer of classes and administrative merger may refer to different units.
No inference of dishonesty or wrongdoing.

sources.title: 100 schools with zero enrolment denotified, 120 merged
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Reports 100 zero-enrolment primary/middle schools denotified and 120 primary schools with five or fewer students merged. Reports difficult-terrain and tribal-area schools were exempted from merger.
limitations: Original school-wise notifications not obtained.
Counts refer to different administrative actions and should remain separate.
Zero enrolment and low enrolment are the official rationale reported; no matched catchment population evidence establishes a contradiction.

sources.title: Krishna Kumari and others v State of UP — 2025:AHC-LKO:38113
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Paragraph 3 identifies Government Order 16 June 2025 and consequent 24 June 2025 list of 105 schools challenged in petitions.
limitations: Exa extract reviewed through early statutory discussion; final disposition not independently extracted.
Subsequent appeal reporting exists; do not present this as final current case status.

sources.title: Documents & Reports — Samagra Shiksha PAB minutes
sources.publisher: Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Provides state/UT financial-year entries with minutes, supplementary minutes, addenda and revisions.
limitations: An index to retrieve further records, not extracted transaction coverage.
Document links may move; origin link health must be checked.
Index includes organisations as well as states, so row count is not geographic coverage.

sources.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
sources.publisher: Government of India / Ministry of Education
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Section 12(1)(c) provides entry-level admissions for eligible disadvantaged/weaker-section children of at least 25% in specified categories of schools. Section 12(2) provides private unaided school reimbursement capped at state per-child expenditure or actual charge, whichever is lower, with provisos for pre-existing free-education obligations.
limitations: Not an unrestricted private-school capital grant.
School eligibility, constitutional/applicability exclusions, neighbourhood rules and claims are determined by applicable law and state implementation.
Statutory eligibility is not evidence of payment.

sources.title: Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools — Lok Sabha Question 1260
sources.locator: PDF page 2, PRABANDH table
sources.summary: Provides sanctioned and reimbursed-to-school amounts under RTE for Karnataka for five years. FY 2025-26 sanctioned ₹156.10 crore and reimbursed ₹148.68 crore. Government says reimbursement is timely, based on information from the state. Describes 2018 Karnataka neighbourhood-school exemption.
limitations: Including Bengaluru does not make this city-level funding.
The table covers the reimbursement claim population; do not interpret as uniquely new entry-grade admissions without checking definitions.
Sanctioned less reimbursed does not establish overdue obligations or misuse.
Distinct from central releases to the state; do not sum with Samagra central share as independent money.

sources.title: MCA Corporate Data Management: CSR Data
sources.publisher: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Portal provides year, state, PSU/non-PSU and development sector filters and an implementing agency master. Displayed education sector is combined with differently abled and livelihood categories.
limitations: Dynamic data values were not extracted.
Do not label grouped-sector expenditure as education-only spending.
Heading and filter years differ; verify downloaded report timestamp before publishing totals.

sources.title: National CSR Portal: company-wise project disclosures
sources.publisher: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Schema includes project, sector, state, district, amount outlay in INR crore, amount spent in INR crore and implementation mode. Portal says company board/director reports take precedence if inconsistent. PAN India includes multiple-state projects and centralized funds.
limitations: Captcha and dynamic selection prevent treating landing page as a project extract.
Company registered office must not be substituted for project location.
Preserve PAN India and NEC/Not Mentioned instead of distributing across states.
No recipient-level totals verified.

sources.title: FCRA Online Services: Annual Returns (FC-4)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Official portal provides FC-4 annual return filing guidance, sample form and document requirements.
limitations: Portal landing page proves reporting route, not receipt by a particular school.
FCRA registration or prior permission is not evidence of donation receipt or programme deployment.
Sample-form fetch returned no extracted page content.

sources.title: FCRA Online Services dashboard
sources.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Dashboard distinguishes active/alive association count from annual returns filed across active, expired, cancelled and deemed ceased associations. State breakdown is explicitly for all association types.
limitations: Registry counts are not education NGO counts or funding amounts.
Snapshot may lag and uses legacy place names.
Association address is not beneficiary location; do not map receipts to headquarters as local school funding.

sources.title: World Bank approves STARS to improve India's education system
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: World Bank approved a USD 500 million STARS programme. Programme supports quality and governance of school education in six named states. Loan maturity 17.5 years including five-year grace period.
limitations: Approval is not disbursement or per-state allocation.
Source page extraction metadata says 2021-01-29 but article dateline is June 24, 2020; use dateline.
Countrywide beneficiaries and six-state activities must not be treated as identical scope.

sources.title: STARS implementation status and results report, ISR59758
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Report states cumulative disbursement of USD 196.75 million (39.35%) against the USD 500 million programme. Report discusses programme restructuring and a requested extension.
limitations: Historical snapshot, not current 2026 disbursement.
Do not add disbursement to original loan value.
A request for extension is not proof that an extension was approved.

sources.title: Cabinet approves MERITE with ₹4,200 crore outlay
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Scheme targets 175 engineering institutions and 100 polytechnics. Total financial implication is ₹4,200 crore, including ₹2,100 crore World Bank loan assistance. Government/government-aided technical institutions are expected to be selected.
limitations: National eligibility is not proof every city or state has an awarded institution.
Targets are planned benefits, not realized outcomes.
World Bank share is part of total and must not be added again.

sources.title: Pratham Education Foundation Annual Report 2024–25
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Report describes direct learning programmes and district, city and state government partnerships. Report contains financials and supporters sections. Historical Mumbai municipal-school partnerships are documented.
limitations: Self-reported programme reach is not a school funding receipt.
Historical Mumbai narrative does not prove current city funding allocation.
No financial totals from this report validated; full financial section not extracted in this pass.

sources.title: Educate Girls Annual Progress Report FY 2024–25
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Audacious Project narrative identifies Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar expansion geography. FY 2024–25 report self-reports 285,237 girls enrolled through Vidya. Report describes two temporary learning centres in Prayagraj during Maha Kumbh for migrant workers' children.
limitations: Programme outcomes are organisation-reported.
No city-level monetary allocation established.
The four named states describe a particular initiative, not necessarily the full NGO footprint.
Annual programme reach cannot be summed with individual-school enrolment without deduplication.

sources.title: Educate Girls FCRA financial statements for year ended 31 March 2024
sources.publisher: Foundation to Educate Girls Globally; N. A. Shah Associates LLP auditor
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Document is financial statements prepared under FCRA for foreign contribution received and utilised. Income statement reports ₹1,08,44,95,261 donations for year ended 31 March 2024, separately from other income. Statements are signed 16 December 2024.
limitations: PDF table extraction is fragmented; manually verify layout before treating each expense line as structured.
Organisation-wide foreign donations do not establish donor-by-city or school-level funding.
Upload path 2026 is not the fiscal year or signature date.

sources.title: Akshaya Patra Annual Report 2024–25
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Foundation describes PM POSHAN implementation for government/government-aided schools. Report says FY 2024–25 operations cover 16 states and 3 UTs. Government contributions are reported as ₹42,093.64 lakh and total income ₹85,746.61 lakh. New kitchens include Bengaluru locations, Pilerne in Goa and Kanpur.
limitations: Government contributions include Anganwadi nutrition; not all school funding.
Government contribution is within total income; avoid double counting.
Kitchen city coverage is not equivalent to school-recipient district or a grant amount.
States/cities arrays are documented examples, not full footprint.

sources.title: KKR and PSP invest in Lighthouse Learning
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: KKR funds invest alongside new investor PSP; KKR continues to hold a majority stake. Recipient described as an education services provider/platform. Release names presence in Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR.
limitations: No transaction amount disclosed in the primary announcement.
Do not substitute media transaction estimates as primary-verified values.
Equity in services platform is distinct from donations to schools, ownership of regulated educational trusts, or FCRA contributions.
Presence is not proof investment proceeds were spent in every named city; Delhi NCR crosses administrative borders.
Delhi-NCR presence is a regional label; it does not establish a school or spending location within Delhi's administrative boundary.

sources.title: Tata Trusts Annual Report 2024–25
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Grant disbursal table reports ₹247.47 crore education institutional/direct implementation spend and ₹40.91 crore education individual grants. Report explicitly distinguishes institutional grants from individual grants.
limitations: No city/state allocation derived from aggregate table.
Institutional/direct implementation spend is broader than unrestricted school grants.
These amounts should not be combined with NGO recipient disclosures without donor-recipient deduplication.

sources.title: HDFC Bank Parivartan CSR Report FY 2024–25
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: CSR education work includes remedial learning, teacher training, scholarships and safe school infrastructure. ECSS supports continuation of education for economically vulnerable students. Projects implemented directly or through empanelled partners; disclosures also appear in directors' report and MCA filings.
limitations: ₹1,068.03 crore report total covers all CSR sectors, not education alone; exclude from education totals.
Report reach across 28 states/8 UTs refers to overall CSR, not proof of education spend in every jurisdiction.
Current open scholarship applications or eligibility deadlines not verified here.

sources.title: Azim Premji University Bengaluru Annual Report 2024–25
sources.locator: Read linked original source
sources.summary: Report identifies the university as not-for-profit, private and established under a Karnataka Act. Azim Premji Foundation is named sponsoring body. Report provides institutional teaching and research context.
limitations: No university donation or scholarship amount validated in this extraction.
Private university status does not imply eligibility for private equity distribution.
Do not generalize one institution's funding arrangements to all private colleges.

sources.title: Drought Condition Assessment: September and June–September 2023
sources.publisher: India Meteorological Department, Climate Research and Services
sources.locator: Summary; Figures 1–6; Tables 1–3
sources.summary: IMD combines SPI, SPEI and aridity anomaly indicators in a district assessment. Summary reports dry/arid classifications from multiple drought indices. District names and indicator-specific tables are provided; classifications are historical.
limitations: Publication date not stated in fetched text; period is not a publication date.
Extracted text includes a September 2022 table caption within the 2023 report and an implausible 30 states / 11 UTs phrase. Reconcile against original pages before loading numerical tables.
Meteorological indicators do not establish household tap reliability or an administrative drought declaration.

sources.title: Monthly Hydroclimate Summary Bulletin: June 2026
sources.locator: Summary; sections 1.1–1.2, 2.1–2.2 and 3.1–3.2
sources.summary: District hydroclimate bulletin reports SPI, SPEI, aridity, rainfall and temperature for June 2026. The document explicitly identifies June 2026 and separates SPI, SPEI and AAI. It provides maps and region-wise district classifications.
limitations: Undated mutable bulletin URL; retrieved content is June 2026, not October conditions.
Extracted SPI region rows and All India extreme-wet totals do not reconcile. Verify PDF/table extraction before any district count metric.
Rainfall and hydroclimate classifications alone are not village drought declarations.

sources.title: Statement on the Climate of India during 2025
sources.locator: Press release header; Highlights; Rainfall section
sources.summary: National climate statement with regional rainfall differences and documented extreme-weather events. All-India annual rainfall is reported as 1,274 mm and 110% of the 1971–2020 long-period average. Southwest monsoon rainfall is reported as 127% of LPA for Northwest India and 80% for East & Northeast India, illustrating why national surplus does not rule out regional shortfall.
limitations: National and homogeneous-region aggregates do not establish city/village conditions.
Document says extreme-weather casualties use media and disaster-management reports; avoid treating every casualty as a direct instrument measurement.

sources.title: Rainfall Statistics of India – 2024
sources.locator: Annual sub-divisional rainfall map; report title page; forewords
sources.summary: Official compilation of monthly, seasonal and annual 2024 rainfall. Report identifier is ESSO/MoES/IMD/HS/Rainfall Report/02(2025)/66. Annual map reports all-India rainfall 1,206.6 mm against 1,160.0 mm normal, a rounded 4% departure.
limitations: Publication year is 2025 in report identifier; exact publication day is not stated in extracted opening pages.
Fetched URL contains a session token and may require replacing with a stable official locator.
Only opening pages were fetched; no district observations have been transcribed.

sources.title: State-wise Annual Climate Statements, 2021–2024
sources.publisher: India Meteorological Department, Climate Research and Services
sources.locator: Introductory description and year/state selectors
sources.summary: Discovery route to state climate statements covering temperature, rainfall, SPI and extreme-weather impacts. Portal says the 2021 state climate statements were first prepared in 2022. Selectors show 2021–2024 and state names.
limitations: Discovery index, not an ingested state-level dataset.
2021 annual documents partly precede the requested window beginning 2021-10-06; finer-period records are needed to filter strictly.
No individual state report values were extracted in this workstream.

sources.title: CWC reservoir storage bulletin archive: 2024 snapshots
sources.locator: Reservoirs Storage Bulletin table; page last-updated label
sources.summary: Official directory lists dated live-storage reports for 150 monitored reservoirs. Visible index includes 21 March, 28 March, 25 April and 13 June 2024 bulletins. Page text says last updated 14 June 2024.
limitations: Archive snapshot is stale relative to October 2026; this is not live storage.
Underlying reservoir PDFs were not individually fetched; no reservoir volume is asserted.
Monitored reservoirs are not a census of every local tank, village source or groundwater aquifer.

sources.title: CWC Flood Forecast portal
sources.locator: Portal title
sources.summary: Official source discovery for river-level and inflow forecasts. Fetched page identifies itself as CWC Flood Forecast.
limitations: JavaScript portal returned no station observations, issue times or validity data to the text fetch.
No current flood status or live alert can be inferred from this record.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Gazette: cyclone- and flood-affected districts declaration
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Revenue and Disaster Management Department
sources.locator: G.O. Ms. No. 604; pages 1–3; paragraph 3
sources.summary: G.O. 604 formally declares named cyclone- and flood-affected districts in December 2023. Order declares Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu and Kancheepuram cyclone affected. It declares six southern districts flood affected and describes damage to crops and water-supply infrastructure.
limitations: Historical declaration is not a present warning.
Rainfall quantities in the order require station/aggregation interpretation before numerical reuse; only declaration and described impacts used here.

sources.title: NRSC Michaung inundation map: 7 December 2023
sources.locator: NRSC/DMSG/2023/CY/TN/01; Tables 1–2; Disclaimer
sources.summary: Rapid satellite inundation mapping provides a historical footprint with explicit uncertainty. Table 2 totals 148,360 hectares of mapped inundation/standing water over listed districts. Report requests field feedback and says no ground verification was done.
limitations: Preliminary rapid map; inundation can include rain accumulation or water in paddy fields.
Satellite scale, resolution, date and interpretation limit conclusions; mapped water is not automatically crop loss or unsafe drinking water.
Acquisition time zone is unstated; do not append IST without confirmation.

sources.title: IIT Madras assessment of Ennore oil spill, filed with TNPCB report at NGT
sources.publisher: IIT Madras / Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board; hosted by National Green Tribunal
sources.locator: O.A. 180/2023 and 183/2023; report title page; Executive Summary; section 2, Zone 11
sources.summary: Technical assessment describes flood-driven industrial oil contamination of waterways and adjoining residential areas. Report maps contamination zones and says affected open wells are groundwater sources. Executive summary calls for remediation and further assessment of prolonged exposure via air, water and fish.
limitations: Technical report filed in proceedings is not a final court finding or a present water-quality clearance.
Avoid adding oil mass and oily-sludge mass as comparable quantities; report itself uses different estimates and discusses uncertainty.
March 2024 is the report month; exact filing/publication day not established.

sources.title: Bengaluru facing 500 MLD shortfall, Chief Minister says
sources.locator: Opening paragraphs; quoted demand/supply breakdown; outer-zone paragraph
sources.summary: Reporting attributes a quantified water deficit and borewell stress to Karnataka's Chief Minister. Chief Minister is quoted giving demand 2,600 MLD, Cauvery supply 1,450 MLD, groundwater supply 650 MLD and shortfall 500 MLD. He said 6,900 of 14,000 government borewells had dried and named outer areas without Cauvery service as affected.
limitations: Attributed official statements reported by news; not independently audited measurements.
A city-wide average cannot establish supply at a selected ward or village.
Historical March 2024 snapshot, not current 2026 supply.

sources.title: BWSSB chairman interview on drinking-water reserves and peripheral shortages
sources.locator: Interview answers on crisis extent, reservoir reserves and treated water
sources.summary: Utility response distinguishes basin water available for drinking from shortages in areas reliant on borewells. BWSSB chairman said 110 villages relied on borewells and groundwater levels had fallen. He said basin storage would be sufficient for drinking needs until monsoon and urged treated-water use for other purposes.
limitations: Utility official's attributed assessment is not independent verification of every household's supply.
Different dates, service boundaries and drinking/non-drinking scopes must be aligned before comparing with other estimates.
An expectation about future supply in March 2024 is an expired historical statement.

sources.title: Families, schools and hospitals describe Bengaluru water shortage
sources.locator: Resident interviews; school and hospital paragraphs; reporter's qualification
sources.summary: Local reporting documents reported interruptions, tanker dependence and pressure on schools and a hospital. Residents in Krishnanapalya describe shortened Cauvery supply. Inspire Public School in Thanisandra and Sai Hospital in Hegde Nagar report dry borewells and dependence on tankers. Article explicitly says a reported 1,500-foot borewell-depth claim could not be independently verified.
limitations: Interviews are qualitative community evidence and are not a representative city survey.
Keep named institution and neighbourhood scope; reported tanker prices need delivery date/volume/radius matching.
Do not reuse the unverified borewell depth as a measurement.

sources.title: IMD press release: May 23, 2024 weather outlook
sources.locator: Press-release header; Subject items i–iii
sources.summary: Archived bulletin demonstrates timestamped forecast evidence, including cyclone and heatwave expectations. Issued May 23, 2024 at 1410 IST. Subject forecasts a cyclonic storm approaching Bangladesh/adjoining West Bengal by May 26 evening and heatwave conditions over named regions during the next five days.
limitations: Expired forecast; it is neither evidence that all predicted impacts occurred nor a current alert.
Different hazards have different valid windows. No single precise expiry time is stated for the whole release.
Use observed follow-up bulletins to evaluate forecast outcomes.

sources.title: Manual for Drought Management, December 2016
sources.publisher: Government of India, Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare; mirrored by PreventionWeb
sources.locator: Title page; Contents; foreword
sources.summary: Government manual provides historical drought-monitoring and response methodology. Title page identifies December 2016 and the Government of India agriculture department. Manual concerns monitoring, drought declaration, relief and mitigation.
limitations: Outside 2021-10-06 to 2026-10-06 evidence window; include only as clearly marked background.
Fetched from an intergovernmental disaster-information mirror, not the original ministry host.
Only opening portion fetched; current amendments and applicable state rules must be checked before operational use.

sources.title: Cuttack block-wise Agromet Advisory, July 1–5, 2025
sources.publisher: IMD Gramin Krishi Mausam Sewa / District Agromet Unit, KVK Cuttack, ICAR-NRRI
sources.locator: Title page; NDVI/SPI page; Athagad and Badamba forecast-period and General Advisory sections
sources.summary: Expired block-level advisory links forecast rain to rice nursery drainage, irrigation timing and crop stages. Athagad and Badamba sections explicitly say forecast period from today 08:30 IST to July 6, 2025 08:30 IST. General advice discusses draining excess water from rice nurseries, delaying irrigation and weather-dependent farm operations. The bulletin separately dates NDVI to June 12–18 and SPI to May 29–June 25, 2025.
limitations: Historical expired advice, not present planting or chemical-use instructions.
Issue clock time is not stated; 08:30 is the forecast-period boundary, not necessarily issuance time.
Block advisory cannot be relabelled as village field conditions or proof that a pest/disease occurred.

sources.title: SATHI: seed lifecycle and traceability
sources.publisher: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / NIC
sources.locator: About Us; Features; Modules
sources.summary: SATHI describes seed production, certification, licensing, inventory, sale and traceability across generations. Digital field inspections and laboratory workflows support certification.
limitations: Portal describes capabilities, not universal adoption or verified seed quality for any village.
A seed tag identifies a batch; certification does not guarantee yield in every climate.

sources.title: SATHI services and onboarded-state statistics
sources.publisher: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / NIC
sources.locator: Certified Seed Production; Statistics of Onboarded States
sources.summary: Service page distinguishes registered area, processed/tested/certified quantities and seed sold. Page notes repeat tests can affect tested-versus-processed quantity comparisons.
limitations: Fetched statistics contain unresolved template variables; no numeric seed stock or state coverage was extracted.
Do not treat blank templates as zero or compare different processing stages as shrinkage.

sources.title: Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Annual Report 2024–25
sources.locator: Section 1.6 Table 4; section 5.4.2 Tables 2–3/Figure 2; section 5.4.6; chapter 20 pp.201–205
sources.summary: Table 4 reports national rice, wheat and pulses area, production and yield for 2021–22 to 2023–24. Section 5.4.2 reports 2023–24 third advance horticulture estimates: vegetables 11.17 million ha, 205.80 million tonnes, 18.42 tonnes/ha. Section 5.4.6 records May 2024 training for farmers from named Nagaland villages and July 2024 horticulture-officer training in Shillong.
limitations: Report is historical and mixes final, advance and cumulative series; retain each observation's own version and period.
National crop totals cannot be allocated to states, cities or villages.
Origin download returned HTTP 403; statements rely on official-domain indexed text. Exa extraction extended to 500,000 characters, selected sections reviewed.
Village training examples do not establish village production, water access, funding receipt or programme impact.

sources.title: ICAR Annual Report 2024–25: crop improvement and seed production
sources.publisher: Indian Council of Agricultural Research / DARE
sources.locator: Salient Achievements 2024–25, Crop Improvement and Management
sources.summary: Report highlights 524 notified/released field-crop varieties and hybrids, including 79 for abiotic stresses. Summary reports 106,397.6 quintals breeder seed produced against indent of 62,104.7 quintals, and 428,046 quintals quality seed including foundation, certified and truthfully labelled classes.
limitations: ICAR reported output is not all-India commercial seed production or seed actually delivered to every farmer.
Variety release, breeder-seed production, certification and retail seed availability are different stages.
Do not promise stress resistance or yield without variety-specific adaptation recommendations.

sources.title: Drip and sprinkler irrigation through PMKSY — Lok Sabha Q2767
sources.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / Lok Sabha
sources.locator: Answer parts (a)–(e), two-page parliamentary answer
sources.summary: PDMC moved from PMKSY to PM-RKVY from FY 2022–23. Government reports 96.97 lakh ha micro-irrigation coverage: 46.37 lakh ha drip and 50.60 lakh ha sprinkler. Assistance is 55% of unit cost for small/marginal farmers and 45% for others.
limitations: Cumulative coverage begins before the requested five-year window and is labelled historical cumulative.
Area covered is not measured water saved, crop yield impact or reliable current system operation.
Do not confuse PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana with PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana, which shares the acronym PMKSY.

sources.title: Progress made under PMKSY — Lok Sabha starred Q165
sources.publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti / Lok Sabha
sources.locator: Answer (a) table; (b) Annexure; (d) Dahod PDMC/WDC paragraph
sources.summary: Answer distinguishes irrigation potential created, command area developed and micro-irrigation coverage. Reports 114.60 lakh ha cumulative PDMC coverage since 2015–16. Reports 14,071 ha under PDMC in Dahod district and two watershed projects covering 15,785 ha; states no AIBP/HKKP project in Dahod Lok Sabha constituency.
limitations: Dahod district and parliamentary constituency are not identical geographies; no-project finding is component-specific.
Irrigation potential, actual water delivery and sustainably available water are not interchangeable.
Programme totals cannot show effectiveness in a village; cumulative and three-year figures must remain separate.

sources.title: Economic Survey 2025–26 Table 1.18: leading crop-producing states
sources.publisher: Economic Survey / Ministry of Finance; ES&E Division DA&FW
sources.locator: Statistical Appendix Table 1.18, printed pp.43–44 / PDF pp.1–2
sources.summary: Official table lists the top three producing states by crop, including rice, wheat and total pulses. Rice: UP 20.76, Telangana 17.45, West Bengal 16.02 million tonnes; wheat: UP 35.65, MP 24.51, Punjab 17.99 million tonnes. Total pulses: MP 5.24, Maharashtra 5.04, Rajasthan 3.93 million tonnes.
limitations: Top-three table is not an all-state crop inventory and absent states are not zero producers.
Crop groups overlap with constituent crops; do not sum pulses and gram/tur or rice and total foodgrains.
Cotton/jute table rows use million bales, not million tonnes; those rows were excluded from normalized observations.

sources.title: Second advance estimates of major agricultural crops, 2024–25
sources.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / PIB
sources.locator: Posted date; methodology paragraphs; crop-wise estimate table
sources.summary: Release describes estimate construction using state crop-area data, remote sensing, crop-weather review and crop-cutting experiments. Published quantities are an advance-estimate vintage, not final harvest outcomes.
limitations: This March 2025 estimate is historical and superseded by later vintages; do not present as latest 2024–25 final output.
Kharif, Rabi and annual quantities must be aligned; estimate revision is not automatically a reporting irregularity.

sources.title: Crop failure assistance: PMFBY premium support and claims
sources.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / PIB
sources.locator: Opening paragraphs; Digiclaim bullet; Annexure PMFBY & RWBCIS
sources.summary: Release separates government premium subsidy from claims paid under PMFBY and RWBCIS. Digiclaim module is described as operational for claims from Kharif 2022; crop-cutting experiments and technology-based yield estimation support assessment.
limitations: Insurance premium subsidy is not identical to a farmer's claim payment or measured crop loss.
Table extraction omits some row labels; no monetary rows from the malformed annexure were normalized.
Claims depend on season, insured crop, notification, coverage, assessment and settlement cutoff; applications are not necessarily unique farmers.

sources.title: Rationalisation of Fertilizer Subsidy — Lok Sabha Q3255
sources.publisher: Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers / Lok Sabha
sources.locator: Answer (a)–(e), paragraph on DBT and geographic disbursement
sources.summary: Answer says fertilizer subsidy is released to companies based on actual authenticated retail sales. Government states subsidy funds are not allocated or disbursed on a district- or state-wise basis, so that allocation data is not maintained. iFMS monitors movement, supply, dispatch, stock and allocation status.
limitations: Do not invent state fertilizer subsidy amounts from national company payments or from quantities supplied.
Subsidized sale, warehouse stock, agronomic need and farmer access are different measures.
Published matrix extraction is malformed; financial values not normalized.

sources.title: eNAM AGMARKNET market-price dashboard
sources.publisher: Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
sources.locator: AGMARKNET Price Dashboard fields/table headers
sources.summary: Dashboard supports state, district, APMC, commodity and date filters. Schema distinguishes arrivals, quantity traded, commodity variety, min/modal/max price, unit and observation date.
limitations: Only schema and selectors were retrieved; no current price observation was verified.
Mandi arrivals are flows through reporting markets, not local crop production, household availability or consumption.
Modal prices are neither guaranteed MSP receipts nor complete retail food-price series.

sources.title: AGMARKNET commodity-wise, market-wise daily report
sources.publisher: Directorate of Marketing & Inspection / Government of India
sources.locator: Commodity-wise, Market-wise Daily Report; Price/Arrival selector
sources.summary: Report separates price, arrivals or both and offers commodity and market discovery. Commodity list includes rice/wheat/pulses, vegetables and fruits.
limitations: Daily report values and observation dates require explicit query/export validation before charting.
No source farm or village origin can be inferred from market location.
Missing reports are not zero arrivals; market unit and grade must be retained.

sources.title: Department of Food and Public Distribution Annual Report 2024–25
sources.locator: Vision/Mission/Objectives; chapter 1 functions and quality control
sources.summary: Department responsibilities span MSP procurement, movement, storage and distribution under food security policy. FCI and state agencies serve distinct procurement/storage/distribution roles. Quality-control cells and grain-analysis facilities monitor specifications and storage quality.
limitations: Responsibilities and aggregate operations do not establish adequate access, quality or entitlements in every locality.
PDS allocation, lifting/offtake, distribution and household receipt are different stages.
Initial extract reviewed was capped at 18,000 characters; no complete stock series extracted.

sources.title: FCI operations dashboard: procurement, stocks, allocation and offtake
sources.locator: Level; Allocation–Offtake; Procurement; Storage tables
sources.summary: Dashboard labels 36 states/UTs and 26 FCI regions. Fields distinguish allocation/offtake, paddy/wheat procurement, due/made payment, capacity, stock and utilization.
limitations: Fetched snapshot lacks a reliable selected-date context and mixes day/progressive counters.
Some displayed ratios exceed 100%; do not call fraud or shortage without denominator, period and system-status reconciliation.
No dynamic amounts published as normalized observations.

sources.title: Building resilient infrastructure for storage of food grains
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.locator: Food Grain Storage Systems sections 1–2; PACS pilot; schemes
sources.summary: Reports 8,815 cold storages with 402.18 lakh MT capacity as of 30 June 2025. Reports 917.83 lakh MT covered/CAP central-pool storage capacity with FCI and state agencies as of 1 July 2025. Describes cold-chain, PACS and Kisan SAMPADA infrastructure; as of August 2025 eleven PACS pilot godowns in eleven states were completed.
limitations: Capacity is not stock, annual throughput, uninterrupted operation or equal local access.
Cold storage spans horticulture, dairy, meat and seafood; total cannot be attributed to vegetables alone.
Announced, sanctioned, constructed and operational facilities require separate status; no complete village storage inventory verified.
Kisan SAMPADA PMKSY is distinct from irrigation PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.

sources.title: CAG: Haryana wheat procurement, storage and delivery to FCI
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.locator: Chapter 3, section 3.4.2 and footnote 8; audit scope section 3.1
sources.summary: CAG section 3.4.2 assessed ₹54.90 crore penalties leviable on transporters for lifting delays in RMS 2020/2021; says none were imposed. Department cited pandemic operating restrictions and efforts to maintain procurement; CAG said no State decision waived the penalties. Audit covered eight of Haryana's twenty-two districts and disclosed incomplete 2020 vehicle data.
limitations: 2025 official archive and February 2025 follow-up support contemporary publication context, but exact publication date was not established.
Audited transactions largely predate the requested five-year window; retain them as older-period findings disclosed in the window.
Audit-calculated levy is not proven theft, a court judgment, money recovered or a current 2026 loss.
Direct-origin PDF request returned HTTP 503; official-domain indexed text was read.

sources.title: CAG Report 20 of 2023: FCI storage management and movement
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.locator: Report 20/2023, section 3.4.3; table of contents places section 3.4 at printed pp.24–31
sources.summary: CAG section 3.4.3 found 10.55 lakh MT owned CAP storage vacant while additional storage was hired in Punjab/Haryana during RMS 2020–21/2021–22. CAG assessed ₹62.76 crore avoidable storage/supervision expenditure. FCI management said hiring anticipated a bumper paddy crop and finalized guaranteed-hiring tenders could not be cancelled without litigation; CAG rejected the explanation.
limitations: Observed procurement/storage seasons partly precede 6 October 2021; do not label as current losses.
Capacity figures are not foodgrain spoilage quantities; audit assessment is not a finding of criminal intent.
Underlying ministry had not replied on this point according to the report; subsequent recovery/action was not established.
Direct-origin request returned HTTP 503; official-domain indexed extract was reviewed through the relevant section.

sources.title: JJM Dashboard: reported and certified Har Ghar Jal
sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
sources.locator: Dashboard; Reported/Certified village explanations
sources.summary: Administrative household tap-connection monitoring and separate reported/certified Har Ghar Jal statuses. Official state, district and village discovery routes are available.
limitations: A connection is not continuous safe supply.
Unhydrated dashboard zero placeholders were not imported.
Live household/village denominators may be reconciled; snapshots must retain dates.

sources.title: JJM Citizen Corner: village information
sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
sources.locator: Choose your village; water quality; village profile
sources.summary: Village search supports water-quality, piped-water-supply, community management and certification discovery.
limitations: Discovery route only; no individual village values were retrieved from this portal.
Village names must be resolved with state/district/subdistrict identifiers.

sources.title: Format J3: tap connections in villages with piped water supply
sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
sources.locator: Format J3 table, columns 3–10
sources.summary: 34 rural state/UT rows provide rural households, balance household tap connections and households with tap connections in PWS villages. The published total is 586,054 villages, 1,935.52 lakh rural households and 1,589.93 lakh households with tap connections in PWS villages.
limitations: Household figures are rounded to 0.01 lakh.
PWS-village households and all-rural households are different denominators.
Administrative connections do not establish regularity, quantity or water quality.
Delhi and Chandigarh are absent; no zeros are imputed.
Exa returned a dated 27 July snapshot; it is not relabelled an October count.

sources.title: National report on functionality assessment of tap connections, 2024
sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
sources.locator: PDF page 18 fact sheet; page 49 quality methods; page 52 section 4.7; page 54 (printed 38), Table 6
sources.summary: Survey covered 19,812 Har Ghar Jal villages, 237,608 households, 761 districts and 34 states/UTs. Table 6 publishes separate regularity, quantity, tested-quality and minimum-of-three index percentages. Section 4.7 explicitly says the sampling design cannot identify the same household fulfilling all three parameters; the published functionality index takes their minimum. Table 6 household-quality assessment uses microbiological laboratory testing and on-site pH; source-water chemical testing is analysed separately in the report.
limitations: Selected Har Ghar Jal villages are not all rural villages.
Published minimum index is not the observed joint share of functional household supply.
The Table 6 household-quality percentage does not establish full BIS chemical safety, including arsenic or fluoride; source-water chemical tests are a separate sample.
Quantity and quality have different sampling units; do not combine as household intersection.
Exact original publication day is unconfirmed; URL folder date is not used as publication date.

sources.title: Assessment of functionality of household tap water connections provided under JJM
sources.publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti / Press Information Bureau
sources.locator: Assessment summary; Har Ghar Jal certification explanation
sources.summary: Release reports 98.1% connections available, 86.5% working, 80.2% adequate quantity, 83.6% regularity and 76% tested water quality in surveyed villages. Certification requires a Gram Sabha resolution after work completion reporting.
limitations: Use the underlying report's sample definitions and minimum-index method.
Published percentages are not universal village or household safety claims.

sources.title: Dynamic Groundwater Resources Assessment, 2025
sources.publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti / CGWB / Press Information Bureau
sources.locator: Opening resource estimates; assessment-unit category paragraph; Annexure
sources.summary: Annual recharge is 448.52 BCM; annual extractable resources 407.75 BCM; annual extraction 247.22 BCM; national extraction stage 60.63%. Among 6,762 assessed units, 4,946 safe, 758 semi-critical, 201 critical, 730 over-exploited and 127 saline units are reported.
limitations: Safe is a groundwater extraction-stage category, not a drinking-water-quality guarantee.
Units generally mean blocks/tehsils/talukas/mandals, not individual villages.
National mean cannot describe every aquifer; extraction includes irrigation, domestic and industrial uses.
All-state numeric groundwater table was not recovered in this workstream.

sources.title: CGWB publications repository
sources.locator: Category and state filters; resource assessment listings
sources.summary: Repository offers state/district and aquifer resources, groundwater quality and resource assessments.
limitations: Discovery index only; report dates, coverage and assessment units need document-level verification.
Direct origin retrieval returned HTTP 503; indexed text was available.

sources.title: Water Resources Information System: India-WRIS
sources.locator: India-WRIS system description
sources.summary: India-WRIS brings together water-resource spatial and temporal information for assessment and planning. Official linked platform is https://indiawris.gov.in/wris/#/.
limitations: Station and basin observations are not measurements for every village.
Check station, parameter, season, datum and spatial boundaries before combining with supply data.

sources.title: National Water Data Portal: NWIC water data
sources.locator: NWIC Water Data description
sources.summary: Water-data discovery spans quantity, quality, use, planning, climate and related infrastructure.
limitations: Portal availability does not imply uniform geographic coverage, freshness or village granularity.
Dataset-specific metadata and access terms must be checked.

sources.title: WQMIS public reports
sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
sources.locator: Public reports WQ1–WQ6
sources.summary: Public report routes include infrastructure/delivery points, remedial action, laboratory capacity, parameters and field-test-kit testing.
limitations: Only report index was retrieved; no contamination counts or clean-water rates are inferred.
Unhydrated dashboard zero placeholders are missing data, not absence of contamination.
Sample time, water point, contaminant and retest/remedial action are required for exposure assessment.

sources.title: Water quality management under JJM
sources.publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti / Press Information Bureau
sources.locator: Water-quality monitoring; interim measures for arsenic and fluoride
sources.summary: BIS 10500 is the drinking-water quality benchmark. Arsenic/fluoride affected habitations may receive interim community water purification provision at 8–10 litres per capita per day for drinking and cooking while permanent schemes are implemented.
limitations: Interim drinking/cooking volume is not the full 55 LPCD household service benchmark.
Policy provision is not proof of installation or safe operation in any locality.

sources.title: Kerala CAG audit, Chapter IV: implementation of schemes
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.locator: Chapter IV section 4.1, Table 4.3; service adequacy and Government reply
sources.summary: Audit reports 2,726 completed out of 5,318 JJM works as at November 2024. 122 of 342 surveyed beneficiaries reported no, limited or infrequent supply. Government response cites 21 lakh additional taps in four years and implementation constraints.
limitations: Survey findings describe the audit sample, not all Kerala households.
Part of the audited period precedes the requested 6 October 2021 window.
Exact publication date is unconfirmed; 2025 report archive path is not assigned as a publication day.
Direct original URL returned HTTP 503; Exa primary-document indexed extract was reviewed.
Audit observations are not a finding of criminal intent and not proof the conditions continue in 2026.

sources.title: CAG Karnataka Report No. 12 of 2025: implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.locator: Section 3.3.1, printed pages 17–18; section 3.5 and Government reply; section 1.5 scope
sources.summary: Section 3.3.1 records incomplete work in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag district during 2024 despite Har Ghar Jal reported status. Government responded in May 2025 that the elevated reservoir was completed by 8 April 2025, with 200 m pipeline and 20 FHTCs remaining before certification/trial run. Section 3.5 discusses 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited/awarded after 31 March 2024; Government cites timely administrative approvals and delays from non-participation and re-tendering.
limitations: Report sample is 28 villages in seven districts; it is not a statewide failure rate.
Har Ghar Jal reported status and certified status differ.
Audit period begins before requested window; Hebbal implementation findings from 2024 and response from 2025 are separately dated.
No evidence of current 2026 conditions or individual guilt is inferred.
Exact original publication day unconfirmed; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 503.

sources.title: Household tap connections provided under AMRUT 2.0
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
sources.locator: First outcome table: Household Tap Connections Provided Under AMRUT 2.0, PDF pages 1–4
sources.summary: Official ULB table reports household tap connections provided under AMRUT 2.0. Selected city rows are retained with original table row and PDF page locators.
limitations: Programme-provided connection count is not the city's total connections or coverage percentage.
No city population denominator, daily availability or quality is inferred.
Municipal jurisdiction must not be silently substituted for district or metropolitan area.

sources.title: Cabinet approves AMRUT 2.0 till 2025–26
sources.locator: Mission structure and City Water Balance Plans
sources.summary: City Water Balance Plans are intended to quantify source, demand, supply and service gaps, feeding city/state action plans.
limitations: Approved programme design is not measured city-level achievement.
Later extensions or revisions need separate dated orders.

sources.title: Government eProcurement System: advanced tender search
sources.publisher: Government of India eProcurement System / NIC
sources.locator: Advanced tender search form
sources.summary: Official search filters support organisation, tender ID, work category and dates.
limitations: Discovery link is not a list of water awards or executed contracts.
CAPTCHA and interactive filtering limit automatic retrieval.
Tender notice, corrigendum, cancellation, award and payment are separate records; no tender counts or award amounts are invented.

sources.title: GeM: all bids
sources.locator: All Bids landing page
sources.summary: Official portal provides bid discovery and warns new or modified bids may take time to appear.
limitations: No hydrated bid results were retrieved.
Procurement discovery is not evidence of an award, payment or misconduct.
Water procurement must be filtered and individual dated documents reviewed.

sources.title: Bengaluru after the water crisis: utility response and conservation
sources.locator: Interview with BWSSB chairman V. Ram Prasath Manohar
sources.summary: Interview with BWSSB chairman describes tanker coordination, conservation and reuse responses to the 2024 shortage.
limitations: Reported stakeholder perspective, not independently audited service data.
Headline 'Day Zero' is not adopted as a verified citywide outage classification.
Projections and uncorroborated numerical claims are not imported.

sources.title: Many Bengaluru apartments continue water conservation measures post the crisis period
sources.locator: Interviews with residents, apartment federation and BWSSB chairman
sources.summary: Resident associations and Bengaluru Apartments Federation describe continued conservation, rainwater harvesting and reuse after the acute crisis.
limitations: Qualitative stakeholder reporting is not a representative household survey.
Anecdotes about reuse do not establish drinking-water safety.
Continued local tanker dependence does not establish uniform city conditions.

sources.title: CAG Report 19 of 2023: Bharatmala Phase I
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.summary: Audit questions project prioritisation, appraisal, elevated design justification and execution. Includes MoRTH replies and auditor rejoinders.
limitations: The ₹18.20 crore/km programme norm and ₹250.77 crore/km sanctioned urban expressway civil cost have different scope; their ratio is not a measured like-for-like overrun.
Primary-host indexed text was read; original PDF retrieval returned HTTP503. Layout repetition/truncation limits downstream extraction.
Publication day corroborated by contemporaneous report; audit period predates much of the publication window.

sources.title: Ministry official disputes Dwarka cost comparison
sources.locator: Article body: cost comparison, procurement and competing infrastructure
sources.summary: A senior ministry official says elevated urban works are not comparable with the corridor norm and describes competitive bidding and appraisal.
limitations: Official is unnamed in the article; this is a reported response, not a signed ministry order.
The article’s aggregate estimate and per-km estimate do not form a clean internally consistent denominator; not used to calculate savings.

sources.title: NHAI letter of award: Dwarka Expressway Package 4
sources.locator: Release paragraph 1–2
sources.summary: PIB identifies Larsen and Toubro as contractor for the Basai RoB–NH8/SPR package, 8.76 km, ₹1,047.007 crore, with two-year construction and four-year maintenance periods.
limitations: Outside the five-year publication window; retained to resolve the historical contracting entity.
Award announcement is not payment, completion certification or the total Dwarka project cost.

sources.title: Bharatmala corridors and state-wise awarded programme snapshot
sources.publisher: MoRTH / Rajya Sabha written reply via PIB
sources.locator: Annexures I and II
sources.summary: Annexures identify 25 greenfield corridors and state-wise total/awarded lengths and tentative capital costs. National awarded length is 26,418 km; awarded tentative capital cost ₹8,53,264 crore.
limitations: Tentative capital cost, award and expenditure are separate stages. Not current status or a contractor ledger.
State rows are programme allocation geography, not company addresses.

sources.title: CAG West Bengal Report 1 of 2026: bridge maintenance and road renovation
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.summary: Road and bridge audit includes utility coordination failures, delayed reconstruction and failed Jagatpur–Dharampota road renovation with departmental responses.
limitations: Exact publication/tabling day not verified; not assigned an invented date.
Primary-host indexed text was read; original PDF request received403. Repeated OCR/layout blocks do not represent repeated incidents.
Test-checked samples are not statewide prevalence or a current engineering safety assessment.

sources.title: NHAI action after Cherkkala slope-protection collapse
sources.locator: Full release, paragraphs 1–4
sources.summary: NHAI attributes slope collapse to design, protection and drainage deficiencies, announces debarment and a show-cause notice for one year/up to ₹9 crore, and says reconstruction is at concessionaire cost.
limitations: Show-cause proposed duration/maximum penalty is not a verified final penalty or present-day debarment status.
No contractor response or final expert committee report was located in this source set.
HAM 15-year maintenance and own-cost reconstruction mean repair does not establish a second public payment.

sources.title: NHAI preliminary report on under-construction Kerala VUP slab collapse
sources.locator: Release body paragraph 1
sources.summary: Deck slab collapsed while concreting on Chengala–Neeleshwaram NH66. NHAI’s preliminary explanation is scaffolding failure; an NIT expert committee was constituted.
limitations: Headline says no injuries; body records one minor injury and no casualties. Body is retained.
This VUP incident is a different asset and mechanism from the 2025 slope collapse on the same corridor.
Preliminary cause is not a final inquiry finding.

The August 2024 parliamentary annexure lists a Kerala NH66 VUP staging failure at km 72+297 (PDF pp. 13–14) and reports suspensions/penalty; the 2022 release does not give chainage, so this is not automatically merged as the same asset.

sources.title: NHAI report on Meachi bridge foundation settlement, NH327E
sources.locator: Full release: structure details, preliminary cause, agency names and inquiry
sources.summary: At chainage 24+461 on the Galgalia–Bahadurganj section, the bridge under construction experienced about 600 mm pile-foundation settlement; the preliminary inquiry considered constricted river flow and scour.
limitations: Preliminary causal explanation and temporary personnel suspensions do not establish final liability.
Release names GR Infra Projects Highway Ltd and project concessionaire GR Galgalia Bahadurganj Highway Private Limited distinctly; parent ownership is not inferred.
No final inquiry report or contractor reply retrieved.
Galgalia and Bahadurganj name corridor endpoints; the exact bridge at chainage 24+461 is not assigned to either locality without geolocation.

sources.title: Parliament bridge/tunnel collapse annexure and actions taken
sources.locator: Annexure I, 20 PDF pages; parent release 2043008 dated 8 August 2024
sources.summary: Official incident table distinguishes existing permanent/temporary bridges, under-construction bridges and tunnels, fatalities and actions taken.
limitations: The source window is relative to August 2024, not the dashboard’s 2021-10-06–2026-10-06 window.
NH/MoRTH reporting scope does not cover every municipal, rural or private bridge.
Different structures and weather conditions require separate reference classes.

sources.title: Infrastructure stability and progress: parliamentary reply
sources.locator: Hindi release 2043008; date stamp and annexure link
sources.summary: Parent release links the bridge/tunnel collapse annexure and explains national highway programme scope.
limitations: Publication provenance for the annexure; not an independent corroborating incident source.

sources.title: Manual for Procurement of Works, updated June 2022
sources.locator: Preface; section 4.9.1A (printed p. 59); section 7.5 (printed pp. 118–122)
sources.summary: Consolidated guidance includes quality-cum-cost selection and debarment procedures; laws and original instructions prevail if inconsistent.
limitations: Generic central procurement guidance; check authority-specific manuals and governing tender date.
Not a new Act, not retroactive proof that an earlier contract violated later guidance.

sources.title: Guidelines on debarment of firms from bidding
sources.locator: OM, 7 pages: ministry-specific scope; cross-ministry procedure; other provisions 16–22
sources.summary: Guidelines separate ministry/entity debarment from cross-government debarment, require an opportunity to respond and preserve contracts concluded before an order.
limitations: Debarment scope, commencement, expiry and allied-firm identity must be read from the actual order.
A show-cause notice is not interchangeable with a final order.

sources.title: QCBS clarification for works and non-consultancy services
sources.locator: PDF page 1, paragraph 3A–B
sources.summary: Clarifies that works of any value may use QCBS following Quality Oriented Procurement procedure; NCS above ₹10 crore require QOP procedure while lower-value NCS follow the specified 2021 route.
limitations: Clarification of 29 October 2021 instructions, not a blanket replacement of lowest-cost selection.
Use depends on prescribed approvals/procedure and the actual procurement.

sources.title: Manual for Procurement of Works, second edition 2025 (final)
sources.publisher: Department of Expenditure; official copy Ministry of Panchayati Raj
sources.locator: Foreword paragraphs 2–3; Preface paragraph 1; parent: panchayat.gov.in/en/document/manual-for-procurement-of-works-2025/
sources.summary: Final edition incorporates GFR, DFPR 2024 and mediation developments. It mainly guides ministries with limited engineering capacity; major engineering organisations may retain approved frameworks.
limitations: PublishedAt records verified republication, not original effective date. The official DoE indexed catalogue lists 5 January 2026 release.
The March 2025 draft is excluded. Subsequent amendments require separate verification.
The manual does not establish improper favour or retroactively rewrite contracts.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh CAG 7/2025: DDUGJY and SAUBHAGYA

methodology: Exact authored relationships only. Navigation paths preserve original arrows and do not imply causation, a continuous payment chain, beneficiary allocation, guilt or probability. An absent link is unknown in this corpus. Amounts are not added across records or stages.
Source-summary corpus, not independently reread original files.
Coordinates are not invented. Entity geography retains the original association basis.
Historical feature availability is not supplied by an event date or publication date alone.
